knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixing sequence is admissible when \(W^k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(\pi^\top W^k=\pi^\top\), and there exist \(C<\infty\), \(q\in[0,1)\) such that \(\|\Phi(k,t)-J_\pi\|\le Cq^{k-t}\) for all \(k>t\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing is admissible when every matrix preserves the intended consensus weighting and every sufficiently long matrix product contracts uniformly toward the consensus projector. children.title: Persistent Network Disconnection
children.top_down_role: Failure of global information propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Network Disconnection
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two permanently disconnected equal-size groups optimize quadratics centered at opposite points; each reaches its local center although the global minimizer is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\) be even and partition the agents into two noncommunicating sets \(V_+\) and \(V_-\), each of size \(n/2\). Assign \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2\) on \(V_+\) and \(f_i(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2\) on \(V_-\). The global uniform objective has unique minimizer \(x^\star=0\). Any protocol whose messages and states remain confined to the two components cannot make observations in one component depend on data from the other; componentwise optimization instead yields \(1\) and \(-1\). Thus persistent disconnection prevents guaranteed recovery of the global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(n\) is even.
No communication path ever joins \(V_+\) and \(V_-\).
Each agent accesses only local data and received messages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=0\), but the disconnected component minimizers are \(x_+^\star=1\) and \(x_-^\star=-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-component quadratic instance showing failure of global information propagation.
review_flags: The explicit two-quadratic counterexample may be constructed rather than stated verbatim in the cited section.

knowledge_statements.title: Poor Network Conditioning
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For symmetric doubly stochastic mixing, the worst disagreement mode contracts by the nonconsensus spectral factor. As that factor approaches one, the communication rounds needed for a fixed reduction diverge at inverse-spectral-gap scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and doubly stochastic, let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n\), and define \(\rho=\lVert W-J\rVert_2\in(0,1)\). For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and every integer \(k\geq0\), pure mixing satisfies \[\lVert W^k x-Jx\rVert_2\leq \rho^k\lVert x-Jx\rVert_2.\] Because a disagreement eigenvector attains the factor \(\rho\), the worst-case number of rounds required to reduce disagreement by a factor \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) is \[k_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\] Thus the worst-case mixing time diverges as \(\rho\uparrow1\), allowing network propagation to dominate optimization progress.
assumptions_latex: \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\), and \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\).
\(0<\rho<1\) and \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k_{\mathrm{mix}}(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil \log(1/\varepsilon)/(-\log\rho)\right\rceil\), which diverges as \(\rho\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral mixing boundary for a fixed undirected network.

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace.
Largest absolute eigenvalue of the mixing operator on the disagreement subspace.

children.title: Incompatible Mixing Weights
children.top_down_role: Loss of preservation or contraction required by a method.

knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible Mixing Weights
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing weights must preserve consensus, preserve the intended arithmetic average, and asymptotically contract disagreement. Failure of any requirement destroys the corresponding invariant or convergence mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^{+}=Wx\), where \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), and let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n\). Consensus states are preserved for every consensus input exactly when \(W\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\), and the arithmetic average is preserved for every input exactly when \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\). If either identity fails, an input exists for which the corresponding invariant is lost in one step. When both identities hold, asymptotic contraction of every disagreement requires \(\rho(W-J)<1\); if \(\rho(W-J)\geq1\), the powers of the disagreement operator do not converge to zero. Thus weights violating any of these requirements invalidate the corresponding standard consensus argument.
assumptions_latex: \(x^{+}=Wx\) is the mixing operation, with \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\).
The intended aggregate is the unweighted arithmetic average.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of \(W\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}\), \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}W=\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}\), or \(\rho(W-J)<1\) destroys, respectively, consensus preservation, arithmetic-average preservation, or asymptotic disagreement contraction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of consensus preservation, average preservation, or asymptotic disagreement contraction under incompatible weights.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixing weights incompatible with a distributed method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a distributed method require a matrix class \(\mathcal W_{\rm req}\) specified by graph support, nonnegativity, stochasticity, invariant aggregation weights, and disagreement contraction. Let \(W^k\) be the matrices actually used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-relative failure: weights can be valid consensus weights for one protocol yet incompatible with another protocol's invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The mixing weights are compatible with the method when \(W^k\in\mathcal W_{\rm req}\) for every \(k\) and their products satisfy every required uniform contraction or joint-connectivity condition. They are incompatible if at least one required condition fails: support feasibility, \(W^k\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), preservation \(\pi^\top W^k=\pi^\top\), nonnegativity, or \(\|W^{k:t}-\mathbf1\pi^\top\|\le Cq^{k-t+1}\) for some common \(C<\infty\), \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixing weights are compatible only relative to a specified algorithm. They must respect the communication graph, preserve the quantity that the algorithm treats as the aggregate, and contract disagreement in the manner required by its analysis. Failure of any required property makes the weights incompatible, even if the same matrices would be acceptable for another protocol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility means \((W^k)_{k\ge0}\in\mathcal W_{\rm req}^{\mathbb N}\) together with the required product contraction; incompatibility is the logical negation of these conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a fixed symmetric average-consensus method, compatibility commonly reduces to \(W=W^\top\), \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), support feasibility, and \(\rho(W-J)<1\).
special_cases_latex: A merely row-stochastic matrix is incompatible with an uncorrected method requiring preservation of the arithmetic average unless it is also column-stochastic.
immediate_consequences_latex: Stochasticity alone is insufficient to establish mixing compatibility.
boundary_notes: Negative weights may be valid in specialized polynomial schemes but are excluded when nonnegativity is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The coupled method is locally stable at \(z^\star\) when there exist a neighborhood \(U\), constants \(C<\infty\), \(r\in[0,1)\), such that every trajectory initialized in \(U\) satisfies \(\|z^k-z^\star\|\le Cr^k\|z^0-z^\star\|\). children.top_down_role: Instability from incompatible primal, dual, and consensus dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Primal-Dual Network Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual network mode diverges when the combined mixing and coupling gain places its eigenvalues outside the unit disk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x^{k+1}=Wx^k-\alpha Ay^k\) and \(y^{k+1}=Wy^k+\beta A^{\mathsf T}x^k\), with \(\alpha,\beta>0\). On a common mode having mixing eigenvalue \(\lambda\) and coupling singular value \(\sigma>0\), the iteration matrix is \[M_{\lambda,\sigma}=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda&-\alpha\sigma\\ \beta\sigma&\lambda\end{pmatrix}.\] Its eigenvalues have modulus \(\sqrt{\lambda^2+\alpha\beta\sigma^2}\). Therefore this mode is unstable whenever \(\lambda^2+\alpha\beta\sigma^2>1\), demonstrating that individually plausible mixing and primal-dual gains can become unstable when coupled.
assumptions_latex: The mixing and coupling operators admit the stated common modal decomposition.
\(\alpha>0\), \(\beta>0\), and \(\sigma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^2+\alpha\beta\sigma^2>1\) implies \(\rho(M_{\lambda,\sigma})>1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modal instability of simultaneous primal-dual mixing.

notation.meaning: Mixing eigenvalue of the selected network mode.
Coupling singular value on that mode.

children.title: Network-Dominated Transients
children.top_down_role: Long pre-asymptotic periods before centralized-like behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Dominated Transients
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a disagreement mode contracting by a factor rho per iteration, the time to cross a fixed error threshold grows at inverse-spectral-gap scale as rho approaches one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(J=\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}/n\), and define the disagreement \(d^k=(I-J)x^k\). Suppose a homogeneous network mode satisfies \(\lVert d^k\rVert_2=\rho^k\lVert d^0\rVert_2\) for every integer \(k\geq0\), where \(0<\rho<1\). For a threshold \(\delta\) satisfying \(0<\delta<\lVert d^0\rVert_2\), define \[N_\delta=\min\{k\in\mathbb{N}_0:\lVert d^k\rVert_2\leq\delta\}.\] Then \[N_\delta=\left\lceil\frac{\log(\lVert d^0\rVert_2/\delta)}{-\log\rho}\right\rceil.\] Hence \(N_\delta\) grows on the order of \((1-\rho)^{-1}\log(\lVert d^0\rVert_2/\delta)\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\), producing a long pre-asymptotic phase above the prescribed network-error threshold.
assumptions_latex: A disagreement mode satisfies \(\lVert d^k\rVert_2=\rho^k\lVert d^0\rVert_2\) for every integer \(k\geq0\), with \(0<\rho<1\).
\(0<\delta<\lVert d^0\rVert_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_\delta=\left\lceil\log(\lVert d^0\rVert_2/\delta)/(-\log\rho)\right\rceil\), and \(N_\delta=\Theta((1-\rho)^{-1}\log(\lVert d^0\rVert_2/\delta))\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-crossing duration induced by slow disagreement contraction.

children.title: Distributed Acceleration Instability
children.top_down_role: Amplification of disagreement by aggressive acceleration.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Acceleration Instability
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Momentum is unstable whenever its characteristic roots for a disagreement eigenmode leave the unit disk, causing geometric amplification of disagreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the accelerated mixing recurrence \(d^{k+1}=(1+\beta)Wd^k-\beta Wd^{k-1}\), let \(v\) be a disagreement eigenvector with \(Wv=\lambda v\). Its scalar amplitude obeys \(a_{k+1}=(1+\beta)\lambda a_k-\beta\lambda a_{k-1}\), with characteristic polynomial \[p(r)=r^2-(1+\beta)\lambda r+\beta\lambda.\] The mode is stable only if both roots lie strictly inside the unit disk. If \(\max\{|r|:p(r)=0\}>1\), disagreement grows geometrically, so acceleration parameters acceptable for optimization dynamics may destabilize network dynamics.
assumptions_latex: \(Wv=\lambda v\) for a nonconsensus eigenvector \(v\).
The momentum parameter is \(\beta\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{|r|:p(r)=0\}>1\) implies geometric divergence of the selected disagreement mode.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Momentum amplification of a network disagreement mode.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, but the cited acceleration and mixing sections do not inspectably support the exact accelerated network recurrence. Moreover, a root outside the unit disk yields geometric divergence only for initial modal data with a nonzero component in the unstable root direction, not for every initialization. A source and a corrected initialization qualifier are required.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncontrolled compressor gain can turn a stable gradient step into an unstable iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For f(x)=x^2/2, choose 0<\eta<2 and Q(g)=cg with c>2/\eta. Then \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\eta Q(\nabla f(x_k))=(1-\eta c)x_k.\] Since |1-\eta c|>1, every x_0\ne0 diverges in magnitude although uncompressed gradient descent with the same \eta is stable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|x_k|=|1-\eta c|^k|x_0|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncontrolled compressor amplification can destroy stable gradient dynamics.
review_flags: This is a failure-boundary map, not a claim that gain amplification is a useful compressor.

knowledge_statements.title: Compression Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar example showing persistent compressor bias and heterogeneity can prevent convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two agents with \(f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-a)^2\) and \(f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x+a)^2\), so the aggregate minimizer is \(x^\star=0\). Let the server update \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha\bigl(Q(g_1^k)+Q(g_2^k)\bigr)/2\), where \(g_i^k=\nabla f_i(x^k)\), \(Q(v)=v+\beta|v|\), and \(\beta\neq0\). At \(x^k=0\), the true average gradient is zero but the compressed average equals \(\beta|a|\). Hence \(x^\star\) is not a fixed point for any \(\alpha>0\); persistent biased compression is amplified by local-gradient heterogeneity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A biased compressor can turn cancelling heterogeneous local gradients into a nonzero aggregate update, so even the true minimizer is no longer a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(a\neq0\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(\beta\neq0\)
\(Q(v)=v+\beta|v|\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(x^\star=0\), the compressed mean gradient is \(\beta|a|\neq0\), so the iteration leaves the minimizer.

notation.meaning: magnitude of local-gradient heterogeneity at the aggregate optimum

review_flags: Concrete counterexample is directly checkable, but no supplied source treats compression failure boundaries.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar construction is internally correct and counterexample is the appropriate kind for this failure-boundary leaf, but no source supports treating this biased map and heterogeneity mechanism as a compression failure boundary.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure boundary for compressed distributed dynamics
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\theta\) collect compressor, stepsize, graph, and heterogeneity parameters for a fixed distributed algorithm. Let \(Z^k(\theta)\) be its state and let \(\mathcal E_k(\theta)\ge0\) be a declared optimization-consensus error.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A parameter-space definition distinguishing exact convergence, error floors, and instability; it does not claim a universal numerical threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convergence region is \(\mathcal C=\{\theta:\mathcal E_k(\theta)\to0\text{ in the declared mode}\}\). The compression failure region is \(\mathcal F=\{\theta:\limsup_{k\to\infty}\mathcal E_k(\theta)>0\text{ or }(Z^k(\theta))_{k\ge0}\text{ is unstable}\}\), where instability means failure of the specified boundedness or convergence requirement. A compression failure boundary is a point of \(\partial\mathcal C\cap\overline{\mathcal F}\), or an explicit inequality in \(\theta\) separating certified convergence from a documented failure regime. A positive finite limsup represents bias or neighborhood failure; an unbounded limsup represents instability. Heterogeneity amplification is recorded when the limiting error increases with a declared heterogeneity measure while other parameters are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compression failure boundary separates parameter settings yielding exact convergence from settings producing a persistent error or instability. Persistent finite error is a bias or neighborhood failure, while unbounded state or error is instability. Heterogeneity amplification means that the limiting error grows with a specified data-heterogeneity measure. A sufficient convergence condition alone is not automatically a sharp failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C=\{\theta:\mathcal E_k(\theta)\to0\},\qquad \mathcal F=\{\theta:\limsup_k\mathcal E_k(\theta)>0\ \text{or instability occurs}\}.\)
special_cases_latex: A bias floor has \(0<\limsup_k\mathcal E_k(\theta)<\infty\).
Divergence has \(\limsup_k\mathcal E_k(\theta)=+\infty\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A parameter value outside a proven sufficient region is not thereby in \(\mathcal F\); actual failure evidence or a converse condition is required.
boundary_notes: The boundary depends on the algorithm, compressor, error metric, initialization class, and convergence mode.
Topological boundary and a merely conservative analytic threshold need not coincide.

notation.meaning: Combined algorithm, network, compressor, and data parameters.

review_flags: This parameter-space definition lacks an inspected authoritative source and should not be treated as a verified sharp boundary.

children.title: Dual-Decomposition Applicability Limitations
children.top_down_role: Limitations involving dual regularity, primal recovery, and coupling structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Decomposition Applicability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-optimal price may leave local minimizers nonunique, allowing independently chosen primal responses to violate coupling feasibility even though the dual optimum is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min\ 0\quad\text{subject to}\quad x_1+x_2=0,\qquad x_1,x_2\in\{-1,1\}.\] Its Lagrangian dual function is \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x_1,x_2\in\{-1,1\}}\lambda(x_1+x_2)=-2|\lambda|.\] The dual optimum is attained at \(\lambda^\star=0\), but every pair in \(\{-1,1\}^2\) minimizes the local Lagrangian at that multiplier. Independent agents may therefore return \((1,1)\) or \((-1,-1)\), both violating the coupling constraint. Thus dual optimality alone does not recover a feasible primal point when local responses are nonunique; averaging or an additional coordinated selection rule is necessary.
assumptions_latex: Local decision sets are discrete and hence nonconvex.
Agents select local Lagrangian minimizers independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dual convergence does not imply feasibility of the unaveraged primal responses without uniqueness or coordinated recovery.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of strict convexity can make the dual nonsmooth and primal recovery nonunique.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample correctly shows that independently selected local minimizers at a dual-optimal multiplier can violate coupling feasibility. However, ordinary averaging is not necessarily a valid remedy here because averages can leave the discrete local sets \(\{-1,1\}\). No source is supplied for the exact boundary claim or remedy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Applicability Conditions and Failure Boundaries for Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(P^\star=\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\{\sum_i f_i(x_i):\sum_iA_ix_i=b\}\), its dual value \(D^\star=\sup_\lambda q(\lambda)\), and local response sets \(X_i(\lambda)=\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\langle\lambda,A_ix_i\rangle\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A definitional classification of when classical dual decomposition is exact and recoverable, and of the principal mathematical boundaries where those properties fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical dual-decomposition applicability region consists of instances for which: \((i)\) the objective and feasible set separate across agents except for a low-dimensional dualizable coupling; \((ii)\) every required local infimum defining \(q_i(\lambda)\) is finite and computationally attainable on the multiplier domain visited; \((iii)\) the dual optimum is attained and \(P^\star=D^\star\); and \((iv)\) primal solutions can be selected or recovered from the response sets so that the original coupling residual vanishes. An instance lies beyond the exact applicability boundary if any of these defining properties fails, including a positive duality gap, an unattained dual optimum, unbounded local Lagrangian subproblems, or nonunique responses without a valid primal-recovery rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical dual decomposition applies exactly when dualizing the coupling yields independent well-posed local problems, the dual optimum is attained with no duality gap, and optimal primal decisions can be selected or recovered to satisfy the original coupling. Failure of any one of these properties marks a stated boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact applicability is the conjunction of separability, local-subproblem well-posedness, strong duality with attainment, and recoverability of a coupling-feasible primal optimum.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
The recoverability condition may be expressed as existence of \(\lambda^\star\in\arg\max q\) and selections \(x_i^\star
i X_i(\lambda^\star)\) satisfying \(\sum_iA_ix_i^\star=b\).
special_cases_latex: Convex problems satisfying an appropriate constraint qualification commonly fall inside the strong-duality portion of the region.
Nonconvex separable problems may retain a decomposable dual while lying outside exact applicability because \(P^\star>D^\star\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A converged multiplier is not an exact primal certificate unless a feasible optimal selection from the local response sets is also available.
boundary_notes: The definition classifies exact use; approximate dual bounds may remain useful outside it.
Communication failures are operational boundaries and are not included in this mathematical classification.

notation.meaning: Agent i's local Lagrangian response set.

review_flags: This synthesized boundary classification requires a source explicitly supporting all four conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Applicability Conditions and Failure Boundaries for Dual Decomposition
Topology-Change Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all changing topologies preserve the same separation into two groups, distinct group constants remain distinct and global consensus is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(G_t\) contain edges only within \(V_1\) and within \(V_2\), although those internal edges may change arbitrarily with \(t\). Initialize \(x_i^0=0\) for \(i\in V_1\) and \(x_i^0=1\) for \(i\in V_2\), and apply \(x^{t+1}=W_tx^t\), where each \(W_t\) is row-stochastic and supported on \(G_t\). Then \(x_i^t=0\) on \(V_1\) and \(x_i^t=1\) on \(V_2\) for all \(t\). Hence topology variation alone cannot ensure global consensus when no finite window joins the persistent components.
assumptions_latex: \(V=V_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}V_2\) with nonempty \(V_1\) and \(V_2\).
Every mixing matrix \(W_t\) is supported only within the two groups and preserves constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global consensus cannot be guaranteed when topology changes never create a jointly connected window.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete impossibility boundary caused by persistent separation despite arbitrary within-group topology changes.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct role, and the persistent two-component construction is a valid obstruction. However, the conclusion generalizes this to every sequence lacking a uniformly jointly connected finite window; that broader absence alone does not imply consensus impossibility because connectivity windows may grow with time. No source is supplied to justify either a corrected narrow boundary or additional hypotheses.

children.title: Execution and Communication Faults
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by delay, congestion, dropout, or unreliable participants.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At logical round \(k\), let \(S_k\subseteq[n]\) be scheduled workers, \(R_k\subseteq S_k\) the workers whose messages arrive before use, \(\tau_{i,k}\) the age of worker \(i\)'s message, and \(c_{e,k}\) the load on communication resource \(e\). Let \(m_{i,k}\) be the received message and \(m^{\rm spec}_{i,k}\) its protocol-compliant value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A mathematical classification of nonmalicious execution departures in synchronous or asynchronous distributed optimization; adversarial message fabrication is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An execution fault at round \(k\) is a tuple \(F_k=(D_k,	au_k,c_k,V_k)\), where \[D_k=S_k\setminus R_k,\qquad V_k=\{i\in R_k:m_{i,k}
e m^{m spec}_{i,k}\}.\] It is classified as omission when \(D_k
e\varnothing\), timing when \(\max_{i\in R_k}	au_{i,k}\) exceeds the method's admissible delay, resource-contention when some \(c_{e,k}\) exceeds its service capacity, and value/execution corruption when \(V_k
e\varnothing\). A failure regime is a sequence \((F_k)\) violating at least one fault bound assumed by the convergence or progress specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Execution faults are classified by missing scheduled messages, messages older than the method permits, overloaded communication resources, or received values that differ from protocol-compliant computations. A failure regime violates at least one fault bound required by the method.

A slow but eventually responsive worker produces timing faults without necessarily producing omissions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The categories may overlap in one round; the taxonomy is not a mutually exclusive partition unless precedence rules are added.

information age of worker i's message

children.title: Uncontrolled Staleness
children.top_down_role: Information age outside the stability regime of a method.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Staleness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a scalar strongly convex quadratic, always reusing the initial gradient makes delayed gradient descent diverge linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=x^2/2\) and apply delayed gradient descent \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_{k-\tau_k})\) with \(\alpha>0\). Choose the admissible ages \(\tau_k=k\), so every update uses the initial point. Then \[x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha x_0,\qquad x_k=(1-k\alpha)x_0.\] For every \(x_0\neq0\), the iterates diverge in magnitude although \(f\) is smooth and strongly convex. Thus convergence guarantees requiring uniformly bounded delay or an age-dependent stepsize do not extend to uncontrolled staleness.
assumptions_latex: The delay sequence is \(\tau_k=k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|x_k|=|1-k\alpha|\,|x_0|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded-delay failure of delayed gradient descent.

notation.meaning: Age of the gradient used at iteration k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is algebraically consistent and counterexample is the correct content kind, but no source is supplied. Because the record uses the example to delimit assumptions in delayed-gradient convergence theory, an inspectable delayed-optimization source must support the delay convention and the claimed failure boundary.

children.title: Straggler Tail-Latency Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Slow participants limiting synchronized progress.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For synchronized round \(k\), let worker completion times be \(T_{1,k},\ldots,T_{n,k}\). If the protocol waits for \(r\) responses, its round latency is the order statistic \(L_k=T_{(r),k}\). Let \(D>0\) be a deadline and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) an admissible deadline-violation probability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic or empirical tail-latency definition for barrier or quorum-based synchronized progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A straggler tail-latency failure regime at threshold \((D,\varepsilon)\) is a completion-time law, or stationary execution regime, satisfying \[\mathbb P(L_k>D)>\varepsilon.\] For a full barrier, \(r=n\) and \(L_k=\max_iT_{i,k}\). A family is tail dominated when a high quantile \(Q_{1-\varepsilon}(L_k)\) grows asymptotically faster than the corresponding typical single-worker latency, so synchronized progress is controlled by the slow-response tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a synchronized round waits for a quorum, its latency is the corresponding order statistic of worker completion times. A straggler tail-latency failure occurs when the probability of exceeding the declared deadline is greater than the tolerated probability. Under a full barrier, the slowest worker determines round latency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathbb P(T_{(r),k}>D)>\varepsilon.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With the left-continuous quantile \(Q_{1-\varepsilon}\), the boundary can be stated as \(Q_{1-\varepsilon}(L_k)>D\), subject to the quantile convention at atoms.
special_cases_latex: For independent identically distributed completion times with cdf \(F\), a full barrier satisfies \(\mathbb P(L_k\le D)=F(D)^n\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Increasing the required quorum size cannot decrease \(L_k\) for the same realized completion times.
boundary_notes: A deterministic slow worker is included as a degenerate latency distribution.
This definition concerns delayed synchronized progress, not stale asynchronous updates.

notation.meaning: r-th smallest completion time in round k

review_flags: No inspected source supports this exact threshold-based failure-regime definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Straggler tail-latency failure regime
Persistent Stragglers
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A persistent straggler exceeds a fixed latency threshold in a nonvanishing fraction of rounds, repeatedly delaying any all-participant barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_{i,k}\in[0,\infty]\) be participant \(i\)'s completion time in round \(k\). Participant \(i\) is a persistent straggler at threshold \(b<\infty\) when \[\limsup_{K\to\infty}\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbf{1}\{T_{i,k}>b\}>0.\] Thus excessive latency occurs with nonvanishing asymptotic frequency, rather than in finitely many exceptional rounds. In a barrier-synchronous method requiring every participant, each such occurrence makes the corresponding round exceed \(b\), preventing any uniform round-time bound below that threshold.
assumptions_latex: Completion times \(T_{i,k}\) are defined for every participant and round.
The protocol waits for every participant at each barrier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistence implies a nonvanishing frequency of synchronous rounds whose duration exceeds \(b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated violation of a finite round-time threshold.

notation.meaning: Completion time of participant i in round k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a terminal notion of persistent straggling, but the proposed definition is unsourced. In addition, a positive limsup gives positive upper asymptotic frequency along a subsequence of horizons; it does not by itself establish a positive limiting frequency or positive lower frequency. A source is needed to choose and state the intended persistence notion.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Latency Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heavy tail with regular-variation index at most one has infinite mean, while synchronous rounds inherit the maximum of all worker latencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonnegative completion time \(T\) is in a regularly varying tail-latency regime with index \(a>0\) when \[\mathbb{P}(T>t)=t^{-a}L(t)\] for all sufficiently large \(t\), where \(L(ct)/L(t)\to1\) for every \(c>0\). The regime has no finite first moment when \(a\leq1\). For \(n\) independent workers with this latency law, the synchronous round time \(M_n=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}T_i\) satisfies \(\mathbb{P}(M_n\leq t)=(1-\mathbb{P}(T>t))^n\).
assumptions_latex: \(T\geq0\) and its survival function is regularly varying.
Worker latencies are independent and identically distributed for the maximum formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(a\leq1\), then \(\mathbb{E}[T]=\infty\), and \(\mathbb{P}(M_n\leq t)=\mathbb{P}(T\leq t)^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularly varying model for severe completion-time tails.

notation.meaning: Barrier completion time for n workers.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: A definition is suitable for the tail-regime leaf, but the first-moment claim is false at tail index one without an additional condition on the slowly varying factor. For example, an index-one survival tail with a sufficiently decaying slowly varying factor can be integrable. An authoritative regular-variation source is required before correcting the exact boundary statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier Amplification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An all-worker barrier takes the maximum latency, so adding workers moves round completion toward increasingly extreme latency quantiles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_1,\ldots,T_n\) be independent nonnegative worker completion times with common distribution function \(F\), and let the barrier time be \(M_n=\max_iT_i\). Then \[\mathbb{P}(M_n\leq t)=F(t)^n,\qquad \mathbb{E}[M_n]=\int_0^\infty\bigl(1-F(t)^n\bigr)\,dt.\] Consequently, the \(q\)-quantile of the barrier time is \(F^{-1}(q^{1/n})\). Increasing the number of required workers pushes the barrier toward progressively higher latency quantiles, amplifying even infrequent tail delays.
assumptions_latex: Worker completion times are independent and identically distributed.
The displayed expectation is interpreted in \([0,\infty]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The barrier distribution is \(F^n\), and its \(q\)-quantile equals \(F^{-1}(q^{1/n})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-statistic amplification at a synchronous barrier.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits and the maximum-distribution and tail-integral formulas are standard under the stated independence assumptions. However, no source is supplied, and the quantile identity requires an explicit generalized-inverse convention when F has atoms or flat portions. A specific order-statistics or distributed-systems locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Slow-Participant Dominance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because synchronous round time is a maximum, one increasingly slow required participant can dominate total throughput despite all other improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a synchronous method requiring every participant, let \(T_{i,k}\geq0\) be participant \(i\)'s time in round \(k\), and let \(R_k=\max_{1\leq i\leq n}T_{i,k}\). Then \(R_k\geq T_{j,k}\) for every participant \(j\), and therefore \(\mathbb{E}[R_k]\geq\max_j\mathbb{E}[T_{j,k}]\) whenever the expectations exist. If one participant's mean latency tends to infinity along a system family, the expected synchronous round time also tends to infinity, regardless of improvements to the other participants.
assumptions_latex: Every round waits for all \(n\) participants.
The relevant completion-time expectations exist, possibly as extended values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[R_k]\geq\max_j\mathbb{E}[T_{j,k}]\); divergence of one required participant's mean forces divergence of the round mean.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round time controlled by the slowest required participant.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind matches the leaf and the maximum-based inequality is mathematically standard, including with extended expectations. Nevertheless, the record has no inspectable source for either the synchronous execution model or its straggler interpretation, so it remains source-dependent candidate material.

children.title: Communication Congestion and Contention
children.top_down_role: Bandwidth sharing and hotspots distorting algorithmic cost.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let communication classes \(j=1,\ldots,m\) inject traffic at rates \(\lambda_j\ge0\). Resource \(e\) has service capacity \(C_e>0\), and routing-incidence coefficient \(a_{ej}\ge0\). Its offered load is \(\ell_e(\lambda)=\sum_ja_{ej}\lambda_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fluid-capacity boundary for steady communication demand generated by distributed optimization; burstiness and queue discipline are not encoded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The uncongested capacity region is \[\mathcal C:=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m:\ell_e(\lambda)<C_e\text{ for every }e\}.\] The communication congestion-contention boundary is \[\partial\mathcal C=\{\lambda:\ell_e(\lambda)\le C_e\ \forall e,\ \ell_{e_0}(\lambda)=C_{e_0}\text{ for some }e_0\}.\] Demand outside \(\overline{\mathcal C}\) overloads at least one shared resource; multiple classes with positive \(a_{ej}\) contend at resource \(e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traffic is inside the uncongested region when every shared communication resource receives less offered load than its service capacity. The congestion-contention boundary is reached when no capacity is exceeded and at least one resource is exactly saturated. Outside the closed region, at least one resource is overloaded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\lambda\in\partial\mathcal C\iff \max_e\frac{\ell_e(\lambda)}{C_e}=1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Defining utilization \(u(\lambda)=\max_e\ell_e(\lambda)/C_e\), the interior, boundary, and overloaded regimes are respectively \(u<1\), \(u=1\), and \(u>1\).
special_cases_latex: For one shared link of capacity \(C\), the boundary is \(\sum_j\lambda_j=C\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A hotspot is any resource attaining the maximum utilization; it becomes a bottleneck on the boundary.
boundary_notes: Finite queues may overflow even for average load below capacity because of bursts.
Protocol overhead must be included in \(a_{ej}\lambda_j\) if it consumes the same resource.

notation.meaning: offered load on communication resource e

review_flags: The fluid boundary is mathematically precise but lacks an inspected source tying it to this node's canonical usage.
knowledge_statements.title: Communication congestion-contention boundary
Network Congestion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If required message traffic exceeds a link's service capacity, its queue grows at least linearly and bounded communication delay is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a communication link \(e\), let cumulative arrivals and service satisfy \(A_e(t)/t\to\lambda_e\) and \(S_e(t)/t\to\mu_e\), and let backlog obey \(Q_e(t)\geq Q_e(0)+A_e(t)-S_e(t)\). If \(\lambda_e>\mu_e\), then \[\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{Q_e(t)}{t}\geq\lambda_e-\mu_e>0.\] Hence backlog and communication delay cannot remain bounded. Any distributed optimization method whose required messages traverse this persistently overloaded link lacks a finite steady communication-time guarantee unless traffic is reduced, rerouted, or service capacity is increased.
assumptions_latex: Long-run arrival and service rates exist.
The link backlog satisfies cumulative flow conservation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_e>\mu_e\) implies asymptotically linear backlog growth and excludes bounded steady delay.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Queue-instability boundary on an overloaded communication link.

notation.meaning: Cumulative traffic arriving at link e.
Cumulative service available at link e.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The overload calculation supports linear backlog growth and failure_boundary is the correct kind. The further conclusion about communication delay requires a specified queueing discipline and a relation between backlog and message delay; it does not follow from the displayed cumulative inequality alone. A queueing or network-calculus source with an exact locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Contention
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Contention occurs when simultaneous worker demand exceeds a shared communication resource's capacity, forcing queuing, serialization, or dropped requests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\) be the set of shared communication resources. During iteration \(k\), let \(d_{ir}^k\ge 0\) be worker \(i\)'s service demand on resource \(r\), and let \(c_r^k>0\) be its available service capacity. The iteration crosses the communication-contention boundary when
\[\exists r\in R:\quad \sum_{i=1}^n d_{ir}^k>c_r^k.\]
Requests must then queue, serialize, or be dropped; hence the communication completion time exceeds the no-contention time even when every physical link remains operational.
assumptions_latex: \(n<\infty\) and \(R\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r\in R:\sum_i d_{ir}^k>c_r^k\) is the contention boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shared-resource contention in one iteration of a distributed optimization algorithm.

notation.meaning: Service demand of worker i on resource r during iteration k.
Available capacity of resource r during iteration k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The locator is specific, but a general communication-aspects section does not establish this bespoke capacity predicate. Exceeded demand does not necessarily imply that requests are dropped, nor that completion time increases when excess work is dropped. The demand and capacity measurement interval also requires definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication Hotspots
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hotspot is a resource whose capacity-normalized communication load substantially exceeds the system-wide normalized load.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For iteration \(k\), let \(L_r^k=\sum_{i=1}^n d_{ir}^k\) be the load assigned to communication resource \(r\in R\), and let \(C^k=\sum_{r\in R}c_r^k\). For a prescribed factor \(\gamma>1\), resource \(r\) is a communication hotspot when

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-cost distortion occurs when measured cost differs from modeled cost by more than a specified relative tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the missing-update set \[M_k:=\{(i,j)\in E_k:a_{i,k}=0\ \lor\ d_{ij,k}=0\}.\] An element of \(M_k\) is a node omission if \(a_{i,k}=0\), a link omission if \(a_{i,k}=1\) and \(d_{ij,k}=0\), transient if it occurs only finitely often, persistent if it occurs for all sufficiently large \(k\), and intermittent otherwise. A distributed omission-fault regime is any sequence for which \(M_k\ne\varnothing\) at some round; it violates an \(f\)-fault model when more than \(f\) relevant nodes or links fail in a required window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A required update is missing when its sender is not operational or its communication link does not deliver within the admitted window. Packet loss with an operational sender is represented by \(a_{i,k}=1\) and \(d_{ij,k}=0\).

Node Crash Faults
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node crash-stop fault permanently removes a previously active worker from computation and communication from some iteration onward.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(V\) be the worker set and let \(a_i^k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether worker \(i\) executes and communicates at iteration \(k\). Worker \(i\) has a crash-stop fault at time \(\tau_i\) when
\[a_i^k=1\quad(k<\tau_i),\qquad a_i^k=0\quad(k\ge\tau_i).\]
After \(\tau_i\), the worker produces no updates or messages unless an external recovery mechanism creates a new active process. This definition excludes transient omissions followed by spontaneous resumption.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is a finite worker set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^k=0\) for every \(k\ge\tau_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Update Omission Faults
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An update omission occurs when a computed worker update is not delivered or applied, without requiring permanent worker failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose worker \(i\) computes a prescribed candidate update \(u_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) at iteration \(k\). Let \(m_i^k\in\{0,1\}\) be its delivery-and-application indicator. An update omission fault occurs when \(u_i^k\) is defined but \(m_i^k=0\), so the server or neighboring workers apply
\[\widetilde u_i^k=m_i^k u_i^k=0\]
in place of that update. Unlike a crash-stop fault, omission at iteration \(k\) imposes no restriction on \(m_i^\ell\) for \(\ell>k\).
assumptions_latex: \(u_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) is defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_i^k=0\) and \(\widetilde u_i^k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transient loss of an otherwise defined worker update.

notation.meaning: Candidate update computed by worker i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The cited asynchronous-update section does not demonstrably establish the proposed omission-fault semantics. In particular, replacing a missing update by the zero vector is protocol-dependent and differs from retaining the previous state or skipping a summand.

knowledge_statements.title: Link Failure Faults
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A link failure removes a nominal communication edge from the effective graph; it is execution-critical when required connectivity is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the nominal communication graph and let \(b_{ij}^k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether the directed link \((i,j)\in E\) successfully transmits during iteration \(k\). A link failure fault on \((i,j)\) occurs when \(b_{ij}^k=0\); the effective graph is
\[G_k=(V,E_k),\qquad E_k=\{(i,j)\in E:b_{ij}^k=1\}.\]
The fault disconnects the entire execution at iteration \(k\) precisely when the connectivity property required by the algorithm fails for \(G_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the nominal graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{ij}^k=0\Rightarrow(i,j)\notin E_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-varying loss of a communication edge.

notation.meaning: Effective communication graph at iteration k.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The effective-graph construction is coherent and definition fits the leaf, but a graph-consensus section does not necessarily support a link-failure fault model. The algorithm-specific connectivity qualification also requires targeted evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlated Fault Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Faults are correlated when their joint component-time distribution does not factor into independent marginal distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Z_{i,k}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate a specified fault affecting component \(i\) at iteration \(k\). The execution is in a correlated fault regime when the joint law does not factor over component-time pairs:
\[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{(i,k)\in S}\{Z_{i,k}=z_{i,k}\}\right)\ne\prod_{(i,k)\in S}\mathbb P(Z_{i,k}=z_{i,k})\]
for some finite set \(S\) and assignment \((z_{i,k})\). Spatially common-cause faults and temporally persistent faults are included; independent Bernoulli failures are excluded.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_{i,k}\) are random variables on a common probability space.
\(S\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint fault law fails to factor for some finite \(S\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence condition for distributed execution faults.

notation.meaning: Fault indicator for component i at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Client Drift
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Client drift is the discrepancy between a client's multi-step local displacement and the corresponding global-gradient displacement; positive gradient alignment indicates conflict.

children.title: Participation and Selection Biases
children.top_down_role: Systematic exclusion or overrepresentation of client groups.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(I_{i,t}\in\{0,1\}\) indicate participation of client \(i\) at round \(t\), with inclusion probability \(\pi_{i,t}(x,\xi)=\mathbb P(I_{i,t}=1\mid x_t=x,\xi_t=\xi)\). Let \(p_i\) be intended population weights and \(a_{i,t}\) the aggregation coefficient applied when selected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order inclusion and weighting taxonomy for randomized federated participation; dependence among clients may require joint inclusion probabilities for variance analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The effective expected client weight is \[q_{i,t}(x,\xi):=\mathbb E[I_{i,t}a_{i,t}\mid x_t=x,\xi_t=\xi].\] Participation-selection bias is present when \((q_{1,t},\ldots,q_{n,t})\ne(p_1,\ldots,p_n)\). It is coverage bias if some \(p_i>0\) has \(\pi_{i,t}=0\); unequal-inclusion bias if inclusion probabilities differ without compensating weights; state-dependent bias if \(q_{i,t}\) depends on \(x\); outcome-dependent bias if it depends on client data or update information \(\xi\); and temporal persistence bias if long-run effective weights \(\bar q_i\) differ from \(p_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A client's effective weight is the conditional expectation of its selection indicator times its aggregation coefficient. Selection is biased when effective weights differ from the intended population weights. The taxonomy distinguishes exclusion, uncompensated unequal inclusion, state or outcome dependence, and persistent long-run misrepresentation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{selection bias at round }t\iff\exists i:q_{i,t}(x,\xi)\ne p_i.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For fixed inclusion probabilities, inverse-probability coefficients satisfying \(a_{i,t}=p_i/\pi_{i,t}\) when selected yield \(q_{i,t}=p_i\), provided \(\pi_{i,t}>0\).
special_cases_latex: Uniform sampling with uniform aggregation is biased relative to nonuniform target weights unless coefficients compensate.
A client with positive target mass and zero inclusion probability has irreducible coverage bias under the given sampler.
immediate_consequences_latex: Biased effective weights generally induce a gradient mismatch \(\sum_i(q_i-p_i)\nabla F_i(x)\).
boundary_notes: Unbiased first moments do not imply low variance or fairness across groups.
Client dropout after selection may be incorporated into the effective inclusion indicator.
review_flags: The full taxonomy and terminology require an independently inspectable source.
knowledge_statements.title: Participation-selection bias taxonomy
Participation Bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Participation bias occurs when the expected aggregate over participating clients differs from the intended population-weighted contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At round \(k\), let \(I_i^k\in\{0,1\}\) indicate participation, with \(\pi_i^k=\mathbb P(I_i^k=1)>0\), and let \(g_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) be client \(i\)'s target contribution. For deterministic aggregation weights \(a_i^k\), participation bias is present when
\[\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^k I_i^k g_i^k\right]\ne\sum_{i=1}^n p_i g_i^k.\]
If participation is independent of the contributions, inverse-probability weights \(a_i^k=p_i/\pi_i^k\) remove this first-moment bias.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i^k\in\mathbb R^d\) is integrable.
\(p_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\sum_i a_i^k I_i^k g_i^k]\ne\sum_i p_i g_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias induced by unequal client participation probabilities.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The first-moment bias predicate is coherent and condition fits the leaf. The inverse-probability correction depends on the precise stochastic relationship between participation and contributions, so the stated independence qualification and weighting claim require a targeted sampling source.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Client-selection bias occurs when the server's conditional selection rule yields an expected aggregate different from the intended client-weighted contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_k\) be the eligible clients at round \(k\), let \(S_k\subseteq A_k\) be the server-selected set, and let \(J_i^k=\mathbf1\{i\in S_k\}\). Given round information \(\mathcal H_k\), client-selection bias is present for contributions \(g_i^k\) when
\[\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{i\in A_k}a_i^kJ_i^kg_i^k\mid\mathcal H_k\right]\ne\sum_{i=1}^n p_i g_i^k.\]
This isolates server selection after eligibility is determined; unequal availability belongs to participation bias.
assumptions_latex: \(S_k\subseteq A_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(g_i^k\) is conditionally integrable given \(\mathcal H_k\).
\(p_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\sum_{i\in A_k}a_i^kJ_i^kg_i^k\mid\mathcal H_k]\ne\sum_i p_i g_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias from the server's conditional selection rule.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The intended distinction between eligibility and server selection is plausible, but no source supports it. The statement must specify which sets, weights, and contributions are measurable with respect to the round information and whether the full-population target on the right is conditional or deterministic.

knowledge_statements.title: Client-Group Underrepresentation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A client group is underrepresented when its expected aggregation weight falls materially below its intended population weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a designated client group with intended population mass \(P_G=\sum_{i\in G}p_i>0\). At round \(k\), let \(W_i^k\ge0\) be the random normalized aggregation weight assigned to client \(i\), with \(\sum_iW_i^k=1\). For tolerance \(\delta_G\in[0,1)\), group \(G\) is underrepresented when
\[\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{i\in G}W_i^k\right]<(1-\delta_G)P_G.\]
The condition compares aggregation influence, not merely the number of selected clients.
assumptions_latex: \(G\ne\varnothing\) and \(P_G>0\).
\(W_i^k\ge0\) and \(\sum_iW_i^k=1\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\sum_{i\in G}W_i^k]<(1-\delta_G)P_G\).

Realized normalized aggregation weight of client i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally coherent and its kind fits the leaf, but no source supports aggregation weight as the chosen representation measure or the tolerance-based threshold. Targeted federated representation evidence is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Federated Objective Distortion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Biased participation replaces intended client weights by effective weights and can move the optimizer, even when all participating clients compute exact updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_p(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i f_i(x)\) be the intended objective and let \(F_q(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i f_i(x)\) be the objective induced by participation. The distortion is \(D_q(x)=F_q(x)-F_p(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m(q_i-p_i)f_i(x)\). It need not preserve minimizers. For \(d=1\), \(f_1(x)=x^2\), \(f_2(x)=(x-2)^2\), \(p=(1/2,1/2)\), and \(q=(1,0)\), one has \(\operatorname*{argmin}F_p=\{1\}\) but \(\operatorname*{argmin}F_q=\{0\}\). Thus biased participation can optimize a different population objective even when every submitted update is exact.
assumptions_latex: There are \(m\ge 2\) clients with intended weights \(p_i\ge 0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\).
Client participation induces effective weights \(q_i\ge 0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^m q_i=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Participation selection can change both the objective and its minimizers: \(F_q-F_p=\sum_i(q_i-p_i)f_i\), and generally \(\operatorname*{argmin}F_q\ne\operatorname*{argmin}F_p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client distortion caused solely by changing aggregation weights through nonrepresentative participation.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports participation-induced objective distortion; a federated-learning source is required.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-client calculation and counterexample are internally correct and fit the failure-boundary container, but no citation supports interpreting participation frequencies as effective objective weights in the intended federated model.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Overtraining
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With heterogeneous client curvature, many local steps can make averaged client solutions converge to a point different from the global optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Local overtraining occurs when increasing \(K\) drives each endpoint \(x_i^{(K)}\) toward a client-specific minimizer faster than aggregation tracks the minimizer of \(F=\sum_i p_i f_i\). knowledge_statements.title: clipping-induced optimization bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Norm clipping generally changes the mean client update. A two-point distribution already yields nonzero bias, so the expected clipped server direction need not equal the unclipped optimization direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(C>0\) and define \(\operatorname{clip}_C(u)=u\min\{1,C/\lVert u\rVert_2\}\), with \(\operatorname{clip}_C(0)=0\). For an integrable random client update \(U\in\mathbb R^d\) having mean \(g=\mathbb E[U]\), clipping targets \(g_C=\mathbb E[\operatorname{clip}_C(U)]\), and its optimization bias is \(b_C=g_C-g\). Thus the expected clipped server update can differ from the intended mean update even before privacy noise is introduced.

knowledge_statements.title: Byzantine-Robust Aggregation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic robust-aggregation contract under bounded honest dispersion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) contain an unknown honest index set \(H\) with \(|H|\ge n-b\), and define \(\bar v_H=|H|^{-1}\sum_{i\in H}v_i\). An aggregation rule \(A:(\mathbb R^d)^n\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfies a \((b,c)\)-Byzantine-robust interface on radius \(\rho\) if \[\max_{i\in H}\lVert v_i-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le\rho\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lVert A(v_1,\ldots,v_n)-\bar v_H\rVert_2\le c\rho\] for every choice of the remaining at most \(b\) vectors. An optimizer using \(A\) must establish honest-update dispersion compatible with this contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If honest updates concentrate around their mean, the aggregator must remain close to that mean despite any allowed Byzantine vectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each coordinate, remove the prescribed number of largest and smallest client values and average the remainder. Different coordinates may retain different clients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(n\ge1\) reported updates \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\) and an integer \(b\) satisfying \(0\le b<n/2\). No iterative state is initialized. knowledge_statements.title: Krum aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krum scores each reported update by its squared distances to its nearest prescribed neighbors and outputs the single update with minimum score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(n\) vectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\in\mathbb R^d\), a Byzantine upper bound \(f\), and a fixed tie-breaking order, with \(n\ge2f+3\). No iterative state is initialized. For each \(i\), let \(N_i\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\) contain the \(n-f-2\) indices having smallest squared distances \(\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\), resolving ties by the fixed order, and compute \(s_i=\sum_{j\in N_i}\lVert v_i-v_j\rVert_2^2\). Choose \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i s_i\) using the same order, stop, and output \(v_{i^*}\).

\(f\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(n\ge2f+3\).

The cases \(q=1\) and \(q=n\) reduce respectively to Krum and ordinary averaging.

knowledge_statements.title: robust update clipping
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip every client update to a fixed Euclidean radius, then compute the weighted average; an empty or zero-weight participant set causes failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given client updates \(u_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), nonnegative weights \(w_i\), and radius \(\tau>0\), initialize the accepted weighted sum to zero and define \(C_\tau(0)=0\) and \(C_\tau(u)=u\min\{1,\tau/\lVert u\rVert_2\}\) for \(u\ne0\). For every participating client, replace \(u_i\) by \(\widetilde u_i=C_\tau(u_i)\). If \(\sum_i w_i>0\), output \(g=(\sum_i w_i\widetilde u_i)/(\sum_i w_i)\); otherwise report aggregation failure. Each submitted contribution then satisfies \(\lVert\widetilde u_i\rVert_2\le\tau\), although clipping alone does not ensure Byzantine robustness.
assumptions_latex: The updates satisfy \(u_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and all norms are Euclidean.
The clipping radius satisfies \(\tau>0\).
The aggregation weights satisfy \(w_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is \(g\), with every clipped contribution satisfying \(\lVert\widetilde u_i\rVert_2\le\tau\).

knowledge_statements.title: anomaly-filtered aggregation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Score client updates, discard those above a declared anomaly threshold, and average the remaining positive-weight updates; reject the round if none remain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given updates \(u_1,\ldots,u_n\in\mathbb{R}^d\), weights \(w_i\ge0\), an anomaly score \(S_i=S(u_i;u_1,\ldots,u_n)\in\mathbb{R}\), and threshold \(q\in\mathbb{R}\), initialize \(A=\varnothing\). Evaluate every score and set \(A=\{i:S_i\le q\}\). If \(W_A=\sum_{i\in A}w_i>0\), output \(g=W_A^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}w_i u_i\); otherwise report aggregation failure. The score, threshold-selection rule, and any data-dependent fitting of \(S\) must be fixed before evaluating the reported round or included explicitly in the algorithm specification.
assumptions_latex: All submitted updates lie in the common space \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
The score function \(S\) and threshold \(q\) are defined for the complete submitted update collection.
Weights satisfy \(w_i\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(W_A>0\), the filtered aggregate is \(g=W_A^{-1}\sum_{i\in A}w_i u_i\); otherwise no aggregate is returned.

knowledge_statements.title: model-poisoning update
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-poisoning update is a Byzantine replacement for the prescribed local update that changes the server aggregate, possibly in coordination with other attackers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) and \(B\) partition the participating clients into honest and Byzantine sets. At server state \(\theta\), the prescribed client rule produces \(u_i=U_i(\theta,D_i,r_i)\in\mathbb{R}^d\), and the server uses an aggregator \(A:(\mathbb{R}^d)^n\to\mathbb{R}^d\). A submitted vector \(v_j\in\mathbb{R}^d\) from \(j\in B\) is a model-poisoning update when it replaces the prescribed \(u_j\) and changes the aggregate, namely \(A(u_H,v_j,u_{B\setminus\{j\}})\ne A(u_H,u_j,u_{B\setminus\{j\}})\). Joint poisoning permits Byzantine clients to choose their replacement vectors coordinately.
assumptions_latex: Every honest client has a prescribed update rule \(U_i\).
All client updates and replacements lie in \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
The server aggregation map \(A\) is defined on all submitted update tuples under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The replacement \(v_j\) is model-poisoning precisely when it is submitted instead of \(u_j\) and produces a different aggregate under the stated comparison.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Update-level poisoning relative to a prescribed honest client rule and server aggregator.

notation.meaning: Prescribed update rule for client i.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition makes an actual change in the aggregate necessary for a submission to count as model poisoning. That is narrower than common intent- or adversary-based uses and may exclude malicious updates neutralized by the aggregator. A source is required to determine the intended definition.

knowledge_statements.title: backdoor poisoning objective
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Attackers choose feasible updates that preserve clean performance while minimizing loss on triggered inputs assigned to a target label.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the post-aggregation model be \(\theta^+(v_B)=\theta-\eta A(u_H,v_B)\), where Byzantine updates \(v_B\) must lie in a feasible set \(\mathcal C\). For predictor \(f_\vartheta\), trigger map \(T\), target label \(y_\star\), and loss \(\ell\), define \(L_{\mathrm{bd}}(\vartheta)=\mathbb E_{x\sim P_{\mathrm{tr}}}[\ell(f_\vartheta(T(x)),y_\star)]\). A standard targeted backdoor objective is \[v_B^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{v_B\in\mathcal C}\bigl\{L_{\mathrm{clean}}(\theta^+(v_B))+\lambda L_{\mathrm{bd}}(\theta^+(v_B))\bigr\},\qquad \lambda>0.\] The feasible set may encode clipping, norm, or protocol constraints imposed by the server.

The clean and backdoor losses are finite on models reachable from \(\mathcal C\).
The displayed constrained minimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any \(v_B^\star\) in the displayed argmin optimizes the weighted clean-and-targeted backdoor objective subject to \(v_B\in\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained update-selection objective balancing clean behavior and targeted triggered behavior.

notation.meaning: Trigger transformation and attacker-selected target label.

knowledge_statements.title: honest-majority robustness assumption
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly more than half of the round's distinct participants must be honest. A fault bound of f together with at least 2f+1 participants guarantees this majority, but the counting condition alone does not guarantee accurate aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a round with finite participant set \(N=H\mathbin{\dot\cup}B\), where \(H\) is honest, \(B\) is Byzantine, and \(n=|N|\), the strict honest-majority condition is \[|B|<\frac{n}{2},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad |H|>|B|.\] If an integer fault budget \(f\ge0\) is declared, the pair of assumptions \(|B|\le f\) and \(n\ge2f+1\) is sufficient to guarantee a strict honest majority for every round respecting that budget. Client identities are counted once within the round. This counting condition limits Byzantine participation but, without an additional concentration or geometric assumption on honest updates, does not by itself guarantee an accurate aggregate.
assumptions_latex: The round has a finite participant set \(N\) of size \(n\).
The sets \(H\) and \(B\) are disjoint and satisfy \(N=H\cup B\).
Each participant identity contributes at most one counted update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The honest-majority predicate holds exactly when \(|H|>|B|\), equivalently when \(|B|<n/2\); moreover, \(|B|\le f\) and \(n\ge2f+1\) are sufficient to ensure it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adversarial robustness boundary for distributed optimization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(P\) be an honest distributed optimization instance, \(A\) an aggregation protocol, and \(\mathfrak A(\theta)\) a nested family of admissible adversaries indexed by severity \(\theta\), such as corrupted-client fraction, perturbation budget, or number of malicious identities. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantee-relative worst-case boundary; cryptographic, privacy, and detection guarantees are excluded unless explicitly included in \(\mathcal G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the robust severity set \[\Theta_{\rm rob}:=\{\theta:\forall a\in\mathfrak A(\theta),\ \mathcal G(P,A,a)\text{ holds}\}.\] The adversarial boundary is \(\partial\Theta_{\rm rob}\); for a scalar monotone severity parameter it is summarized by \[\theta^\star:=\sup\{\theta:\forall a\in\mathfrak A(\theta),\ \mathcal G(P,A,a)\text{ holds}\}.\] Severity beyond the boundary admits at least one allowed adversary that violates the declared guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The robust severity set consists of attack budgets under which the optimization guarantee holds against every allowed adversary. special_cases_latex: The severity parameter may be the maximum number \(f\) of Byzantine clients, an \(\ell_p\) poisoning radius, or the fraction of Sybil-controlled aggregation weight.

knowledge_statements.title: Byzantine Update Faults
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Byzantine client may send any adaptive optimization vector, unrelated to data or the prescribed algorithm, while honest clients follow the protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Byzantine update fault is present when a client \(i\in B\) may transmit an arbitrary message \(u_i^t=\phi_i^t(\mathcal H_t,\xi_i^t)\in\mathbb R^d\) at round \(t\), where \(\phi_i^t\) is unrestricted, \(\mathcal H_t\) is the observable history, and \(\xi_i^t\) permits private randomness. The message need not equal a gradient, correspond to any dataset, or remain consistent across recipients or rounds. Honest clients \(i\notin B\) follow the specified update rule. A robustness statement under this model must hold uniformly over the Byzantine set and all admissible adaptive message strategies.
assumptions_latex: A server expects one update in \(\mathbb R^d\) from each selected client.
The Byzantine set \(B\) is not constrained by the prescribed local algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\in B\), the transmitted update may be any adaptive vector in \(\mathbb R^d\); guarantees must therefore quantify over all such choices.

Data Poisoning Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data poisoning changes an allowed number of client examples, then lets the normal training rule propagate that change into the objective and update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(D_i=\{z_{ij}\}_{j=1}^{n_i}\), a data-poisoning interface permits an attacker to choose \(D_i'\in\mathcal A_i(D_i)\), where \(\mathcal A_i(D_i)\) is an explicitly declared admissible set, such as datasets obtained by replacing at most \(b_i\) examples. The client then forms \(f_i'(x)=|D_i'|^{-1}\sum_{z\in D_i'}\ell(x;z)\) and applies the prescribed optimizer to \(f_i'\). Thus the attack acts through \(D_i\mapsto D_i'\mapsto f_i'\mapsto u_i'\); it does not directly authorize an arbitrary objective or message beyond what some admissible \(D_i'\) induces.
