An attacker may replace \(D_i\) by an admissible poisoned dataset \(D_i'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The data-poisoning interface is the map \(D_i\mapsto D_i'\mapsto f_i'\mapsto u_i'\), with admissibility enforced at the dataset level.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dataset-level attack interface, distinguished from direct manipulation of objectives or transmitted updates.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports a formal federated data-poisoning interface or poisoning budget.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The dataset-to-objective-to-update interface is coherent and definition is the correct kind, but the admissible poisoning model and example-replacement budget lack a supporting federated data-poisoning citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Poisoning Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Objective poisoning directly perturbs a client loss within a declared function class, without requiring that the new loss arise from modified data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective-poisoning interface permits an attacker controlling client \(i\) to replace \(f_i\) by \(\widetilde f_i=f_i+h_i\), where \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\) and \(\mathcal H_i\) states all magnitude, smoothness, convexity, or support restrictions. The client update is then generated by the prescribed local algorithm applied to \(\widetilde f_i\). Unlike data poisoning, the interface does not require \(\widetilde f_i\) to equal an empirical risk derived from an admissible modified dataset. Unlike a Byzantine-message model, it still requires the transmitted update to be consistent with optimizing some allowed \(\widetilde f_i\).
assumptions_latex: Client \(i\) has benign objective \(f_i:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\).
The attack class specifies an admissible perturbation set \(\mathcal H_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Objective poisoning replaces \(f_i\) by \(f_i+h_i\) for \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\), independently of whether the perturbed objective is realizable by poisoned data.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-level poisoning interface before execution of the prescribed local optimizer.
review_flags: No supplied locator establishes the intended objective-poisoning attack class or its relation to data realizability.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The function-level interface is mathematically explicit and distinguished from data and message poisoning, but its attack class and data-realizability distinction are not supported by a cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Targeted Optimization Distortion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A targeted attack succeeds when admissible poisoned objectives make a preselected point approximately optimal while satisfying the stated collateral constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde F(x)=\sum_{i\notin B}p_i f_i(x)+\sum_{i\in B}p_i(f_i(x)+h_i(x))\). A targeted optimization distortion toward \(x_{\mathrm{tar}}\) succeeds at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) when there exist \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\) such that \(\widetilde F(x_{\mathrm{tar}})\le\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^d}\widetilde F(x)+\varepsilon\), together with every declared collateral constraint, such as \(C(h_1,\ldots,h_m)\le\rho\). The target is attacker-selected before evaluation. Without the target condition, merely increasing benign loss or preventing convergence constitutes untargeted disruption rather than targeted distortion.
assumptions_latex: The attacker controls objectives indexed by \(B\) and chooses admissible perturbations \(h_i\in\mathcal H_i\).
A target point \(x_{\mathrm{tar}}\in\mathbb R^d\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A targeted distortion succeeds when \(x_{\mathrm{tar}}\) is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal for the poisoned aggregate while the declared admissibility and collateral constraints hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization-level success predicate for steering the aggregate toward a prescribed target.
review_flags: No supplied source specifies a canonical success predicate for targeted federated optimization distortion.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The epsilon-optimality predicate is precise and condition fits the terminal container, but no source establishes it as the intended success criterion for targeted optimization distortion or supports the chosen collateral-constraint formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Poisoning Detectability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a benign world and a poisoned world produce identical observable transcripts, every detector has false-positive or false-negative probability at least one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be the law of the observable transcript \(T\) in an admissible benign world and \(P_1\) its law in an admissible poisoned world. If \(P_0=P_1\), then for every possibly randomized detector \(\delta(T)\in\{0,1\}\), with \(1\) denoting poisoning, \[P_0(\delta(T)=1)+P_1(\delta(T)=0)=1.\] Consequently at least one of its false-positive and false-negative probabilities is at least \(1/2\). Poisoning is therefore not uniformly detectable from \(T\) unless the model excludes observationally equivalent benign and poisoned worlds or supplies additional trusted information.
assumptions_latex: A detector observes a transcript \(T\) and outputs either benign or poisoned.
Two admissible worlds induce transcript laws \(P_0\) and \(P_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P_0=P_1\), every detector \(\delta\) satisfies \(P_0(\delta(T)=1)+P_1(\delta(T)=0)=1\); uniform reliable detection is impossible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic impossibility boundary based on observationally identical protocol transcripts.
review_flags: The indistinguishability argument is standard, but no supplied locator connects it to federated poisoning detectability.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishability calculation is mathematically correct and failure_boundary is appropriate, but no inspectable citation connects this testing boundary to admissible benign and poisoned federated transcripts.

children.title: Collusion and Sybil Attacks
children.top_down_role: Optimization consequences of coordinated or duplicated malicious clients.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(H\) be a set of honest physical clients, \(P\) a set of malicious physical principals, and \(I\) the identities admitted by a distributed optimization protocol. In round \(t\), identity \(i\in I\) submits a message \(m_{i,t}\in\mathcal M_t\). The server or peer network applies an aggregation map \(A_t:\mathcal M_t^{I_t}\to\mathcal Y_t\) to the messages of the participating identities \(I_t\subseteq I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-client distributed or federated optimization in which protocol-level identities need not correspond one-to-one with physical participants. The definition concerns the adversary interface, not a particular poisoning objective or aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A collusion–Sybil attack interface is a tuple \(\mathfrak A=(P,S,\pi,\{K_t\}_{t\ge0})\), where \(S\subseteq I\) is the set of adversarially controlled identities, \(\pi:S\to P\) maps each identity to its controlling physical principal, and \(K_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal H_t)\) is a joint probability kernel on \(\mathcal M_t^{S_t}\), with \(S_t=S\cap I_t\), conditioned on the adversary-visible history \(\mathcal H_t\). It is a Sybil interface when \(\pi\) is noninjective, equivalently when \(\exists p\in P\) such that \(|\pi^{-1}(p)|\ge2\). It is a collusion interface when the conditional joint law need not factor by principal: for some \(t\) and history \(h\), \[K_t(dm_{S_t}\mid h)\ne\prod_{p\in P}K_{p,t}(dm_{S_t\cap\pi^{-1}(p)}\mid h).\] The effective adversarial weight in round \(t\) is \(\alpha_t=|S_t|/|I_t|\), while the physical-adversary fraction is \(\beta_t=|\pi(S_t)|/(|H_t|+|\pi(S_t)|)\). The interface exposes a collusion–Sybil boundary precisely when protocol influence is allocated by identity and \(\alpha_t\) can exceed \(\beta_t\) because one or more principals control multiple admitted identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface consists of malicious physical principals, their controlled protocol identities, a map from identities to principals, and a history-dependent joint law for their round messages. It is Sybil-capable when at least one principal controls two or more identities. It is collusive when controlled messages may be jointly coordinated rather than conditionally independent across principals. Identity-weighted aggregation exposes the boundary when the adversarial identity fraction \(\alpha_t\) may exceed the physical-adversary fraction \(\beta_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak A\) is collusion–Sybil capable exactly when coordinated kernels \(K_t\) are permitted and the control map \(\pi:S\to P\) is noninjective.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Noninjectivity of \(\pi\) is equivalent to \(|S|>|\pi(S)|\) when \(S\) is finite.
For identity-uniform aggregation, Sybil amplification in round \(t\) can be recorded by \(a_t=\alpha_t/\beta_t>1\), provided \(\beta_t>0\).
special_cases_latex: Pure collusion has injective \(\pi\) but permits a nonfactorizing \(K_t\).
A pure Sybil attack by one principal has \(|P|=1\), \(|S|\ge2\), and arbitrarily dependent messages across \(S_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Any robustness condition stated only in terms of the number of malicious identities constrains \(\alpha_t\), not necessarily the number of malicious physical principals.
Identity authentication enforcing \(|\pi^{-1}(p)|\le1\) removes Sybil multiplicity but does not by itself remove collusion.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require malicious messages to be identical; coordinated identities may submit distinct adaptive messages.
Data-objective poisoning is separate: this interface specifies control and coordination, not how local objectives or datasets are corrupted.
No inspected source locator was supplied that canonically defines this combined interface with the stated kernel and identity-to-principal map.

knowledge_statements.title: Collusion–Sybil Attack Interface
Colluding-Client Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Colluding clients coordinate their updates using shared state and randomness, so their joint behavior need not factor into independent client strategies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A colluding-client interface permits a controlled set \(B\) to choose its round-\(t\) messages jointly as \((u_i^t)_{i\in B}=\Phi_t(\mathcal H_t,S_t,\xi_t)\), where \(\mathcal H_t\) is the visible protocol history, \(S_t\) is shared private state, and \(\xi_t\) is joint randomness. Each component remains attached to a distinct registered client and must satisfy any declared per-client constraint. The defining feature is that the joint law need not factor across clients: \(P((u_i^t)_{i\in B}\mid\mathcal H_t)\ne\prod_{i\in B}P(u_i^t\mid\mathcal H_t)\) may hold.
assumptions_latex: A controlled set \(B\) can communicate privately or share state.
Each controlled client submits one protocol-visible update per round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Collusion allows the tuple \((u_i^t)_{i\in B}\) to follow an arbitrary joint strategy subject only to the declared per-client protocol constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint-strategy interface for multiple distinct controlled clients with shared information.

notation.meaning: Shared colluder state before round t
Update of client i at round t

review_flags: No supplied locator formalizes colluding clients in distributed or federated optimization.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The joint-strategy formulation fits a colluding-client interface and is internally consistent, but no source supports this particular information, shared-state, randomness, and per-client-constraint model.

knowledge_statements.title: Sybil-Client Interface
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Sybil attacker uses multiple apparent client identities, allowing one controller to submit several updates and accumulate identity-based aggregation weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Sybil-client interface exists when one adversarial principal controls \(k=|S|\ge2\) logical identities and may submit an update \(u_s^t\) under each \(s\in S\) during round \(t\). The server observes separate identities but does not observe their common controller. If aggregation assigns weights \(w_s^t\) by identity, the principal's direct aggregate contribution is \(\sum_{s\in S}w_s^t u_s^t\), rather than the contribution allowed to one physical principal. The interface must specify registration, participation, and weighting constraints; otherwise the effective adversarial weight is undefined.
assumptions_latex: One adversarial principal controls a set \(S\) of registered logical client identities.
The server treats identities as separate contributors unless an identity-control rule intervenes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A Sybil interface permits one principal to submit the family \((u_s^t)_{s\in S}\) through multiple apparent clients and thereby acquire identity-dependent aggregation weight.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity-level attack interface in which one principal controls multiple apparent clients.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports a formal Sybil-client model for federated aggregation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The definition clearly separates logical identities from their common controller and correctly notes dependence on registration and weighting rules, but it lacks a source for the federated Sybil threat model.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinated Update Manipulation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Colluders can realize a target aggregate shift precisely when that shift belongs to the weighted Minkowski sum of their individually allowed update sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For aggregation weights \(w_i\ge0\), coordinated update manipulation toward \(b\in\mathbb R^d\) is feasible when the colluders can choose \(u_i\in U_i\) jointly so that \(\sum_{i\in B}w_i u_i=b\). Equivalently, \[b\in\sum_{i\in B}w_iU_i:=\left\{\sum_{i\in B}w_i v_i:v_i\in U_i\right\}.\] This condition captures aggregate coordination even when every individual update satisfies its local admissibility test. If only approximate manipulation is required, feasibility becomes \(\operatorname{dist}(b,\sum_{i\in B}w_iU_i)\le\varepsilon\) for the declared norm and tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
assumptions_latex: Colluding clients \(B\) submit vectors \(u_i\in\mathbb R^d\).
Each vector obeys a declared individual constraint \(u_i\in U_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A desired aggregate displacement \(b\) is coordinately realizable exactly when \(b\in\sum_{i\in B}w_iU_i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-round feasibility condition for jointly producing a prescribed aggregate contribution.

notation.meaning: Allowed update set for client i

review_flags: No supplied locator establishes this coordinated-update feasibility model in an adversarial aggregation setting.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The weighted Minkowski-sum equivalence follows from the declared one-round model, and condition is an appropriate content kind. A source is still required to establish that this feasibility model represents coordinated adversarial update manipulation in the target context.

knowledge_statements.title: Identity-Multiplicity Effects
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under uniform identity averaging, duplicating one update across many identities increases its weight and can force the aggregate arbitrarily close to that update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let honest updates be \(h_1,\ldots,h_n\) and suppose one adversarial principal repeats \(v\in\mathbb R^d\) through \(k\) identities. Uniform identity averaging returns \[A_k=\frac{\sum_{j=1}^n h_j+kv}{n+k}.\] Hence the principal's coefficient is \(k/(n+k)\), whereas a single identity would receive coefficient \(1/(n+1)\). Moreover \(A_k\to v\) as \(k\to\infty\). Thus an aggregator that weights identities rather than authenticated principals is not invariant under identity replication, even when all repeated update vectors are unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The server averages updates uniformly by registered identity.
There are \(n\ge1\) honest identities and \(k\ge1\) identical Sybil identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Duplicating one update \(v\) across \(k\) identities changes its aggregate coefficient from \(1/(n+1)\) to \(k/(n+k)\), approaching one as \(k\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact multiplicity effect under uniform identity-weighted mean aggregation.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports identity-multiplicity effects in federated aggregation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The uniform-averaging formula and limiting multiplicity effect are correct, and property fits the node. No citation supports the identity-replication model or its relevance to Sybil behavior in federated aggregation.
